alert.name: ECSServiceAlarm
alert.summary: CloudWatch alarm fired for ECS service checkout

logs: EVENT BackOff Pod/checkout-6796d89f8c-z6s8z: Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-6796d89f8c-z6s8z_warden-pg(<UUID_1>)
EVENT BackOff Pod/checkout-6796d89f8c-rlskd: Back-off restarting failed container checkout in pod checkout-6796d89f8c-rlskd_warden-pg(<UUID_2>)
checkout-6796d89f8c-rlskd/checkout 2026-09-24T12:49:25.156824395Z checkout: WARN memory pressure rising
checkout-6796d89f8c-z6s8z/checkout 2026-09-24T12:49:25.143196996Z checkout: WARN memory pressure rising

root_cause.hypothesis: Container OOM-killed: app attempts to allocate ~900MiB cache but pod memory_limit_mib is only 48MiB, causing OOMKilled -> CrashLoopBackOff on both replicas. No recent deploy implicated; looks like a memory limit misconfiguration (or a cache-size regression) rather than a code deploy regression.
evidence: metrics show memory_limit_mib=48 vs log 'allocating 900MiB cache' on both pods
WARN memory pressure rising immediately after start, both replicas, same pattern
RECENT DEPLOYS empty -> rules out a fresh bad deploy as trigger
ruled_out: Bad new deploy causing regression (deploy list empty)
Single-pod/node-local issue (both replicas z6s8z and rlskd show identical failure)

proposal.reasoning: Both replicas OOMKilled: app allocates ~900MiB cache but memory_limit_mib=48, so every restart repeats the crash. Root cause is the memory limit vs actual working-set, not a deploy (recent deploys empty). Bumping the memory limit lets the container survive its own cache allocation and breaks the crashloop; restart_pods alone would just loop again under same 48MiB cap.
proposal.expected_effect: Task memory limit raised above ~900MiB+headroom, pods stop OOMKilling, restart_count and crashloop_containers drop to 0, pods_ready returns to 2/2.

reasons: Passed all policies. Held for operator approval before execution.
